name: Sudan Archives
label: Stones Throw
lede: A Cincinnati violinist who dodged a pop-duo career, taught herself beats on an iPad, and ended up on Pitchfork's year-end lists three times.

eras.title: Kicked out of the pop duo
eras.text: Brittney Parks grows up in Cincinnati playing violin by ear, dodges a pop-duo career her stepfather had planned, and lands in Los Angeles at 19 with a violin and an iPad.

years.h: She names herself Sudan after discovering Sudanese fiddlers
years.p: Brittney Parks, a Cincinnati violinist raised on Irish folk tunes, takes the name from the Sudanese fiddling she'd been studying, Stereogum reports.
years.xp:
Parks began violin in fourth grade and learned by ear. Stereogum says she named herself Sudan around 17, after falling for Sudanese fiddlers; she cites Asim Gorashi and Cameroonian electronic pioneer [[Francis Bebey|fab6adab-b46f-45f8-8700-bc44408ba583]] as touchstones.

The mission became a line she repeats in interviews: the violin is a Black instrument, and Western classical training doesn't teach that.

years.src: NPR: I'm different · Wikipedia: Sudan Archives
years.h: Her stepfather, a LaFace Records man, wants her in a pop duo
years.p: N2 was to be Parks and her twin sister Cat; she skipped rehearsals for electronic shows.
years.xp:
NPR reports her stepfather, who helped launch LaFace Records (home to OutKast and TLC), tried to shape the sisters into N2. Parks has said the setup stifled her creativity.

She was kicked out at 19, NPR says, and moved to Los Angeles.

years.cap: Sudan Archives at Codfish Hollow, Maquoketa, IA 8/29/18 · Wikimedia
years.src: NPR: I'm different · Stereogum: The Story Behind
years.h: Los Angeles: ethnomusicology by day, Low End Theory by night
years.p: She studies at Pasadena City College and makes beats on an iPad, then an MPC.
years.xp: At the Low End Theory club night, the Los Angeles beat scene's weekly church, Parks met people from Stones Throw. Stereogum credits label producer [[Matthewdavid|a9549228-8e49-41d2-9a04-0b5ea2056800]] with discovering her.

eras.title: Stones Throw, a violin and a loop pedal
eras.text: Two EPs on Stones Throw, then a debut album that made her a year-end fixture.

years.h: Debut EP Sudan Archives arrives on Stones Throw
years.p: Parks's first release: violin, loops and beats, six years into her Los Angeles life.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sudan Archives · NPR: I'm different
yt: Nont For Sale, live on KEXP
years.h: Sink EP and the single "Nont for Sale"
years.p: Stereogum named the song a favorite of May 2018; she played it live on KEXP.
years.xp: Sink was the second of the two EPs Stones Throw released before her debut album, per NPR. NPR's 2018 profile described her smooth sound as pulling from everywhere.

years.src: Wikipedia: Athena · Stereogum: The Story Behind
years.h: Athena: her autobiography, with a Black goddess on the cover idea
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 7.7; the New York Times ranked it No. 4 of 2019.
years.xp:
Produced by Parks with help from [[Washed Out|74a30f2a-dae6-4e99-8a75-cb0f93b31aa6]], [[Paul White|1e6ee12a-b6dd-4557-99a3-17261bc510f8]] and Will Archer, per Wikipedia. Metacritic scores it 83.

She has said she wanted a Black female goddess because she didn't see any in pictures of Athena. Stereogum calls the record her autobiography.

eras.title: The basement studio
eras.text: Lockdown, a home studio and full creative control produce the record that puts her at No. 2 on Pitchfork's year-end list.

years.p: Her NPR Tiny Desk Concert introduces the violin-and-voice version of the Athena songs.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the Tiny Desk concert in 2020; WXPN covered the June release.

years.p: Pitchfork named it a Best New Track.

years.big: It began as a record called Homesick
q: I have to be in control of it.
years.src: Wikipedia: Natural Brown Prom Queen · Rolling Stone
years.h: Natural Brown Prom Queen: 18 tracks from a basement
years.p: Pitchfork scored it 9.0 and ranked it No. 2 of 2022; the New York Times had it No. 4.
years.xp:
Parks says she built the studio in her Los Angeles basement with then-partner James McCall (Nocando, All City Jimmy) in lockdown. She originally called it Homesick, missing Cincinnati and her mother; the title refers to a prom she missed. Closer "#513" is her area code, with producer [[Hi-Tek|fcb6d9df-6cef-4f33-8850-7570bcc99718]].

Collaborators sent stems and she assembled them herself. "I have to be in control of it," she told Rolling Stone.

years.p: Her network TV debut; the video is one of her most-watched, and she later played it on Austin City Limits.

eras.title: Gadget Girl
eras.text: Awards, a breakup, a house sale and a dance record that trades violin front-and-center for club engineering.

years.h: Two Libera Awards for Natural Brown Prom Queen
years.p: Best Breakthrough Artist/Release and Best R&B Record, the independent-music industry's own trophies.
The single lands months before a record built after a breakup and a home sale, NME reports.
years.xp: NME says Parks made the album following a breakup, a home sale and major upheaval, calling it cathartic. Wikipedia notes she and McCall separated during its production.

years.src: Wikipedia: The BPM · Album of the Year · NPR: In an era · NME · Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2025
years.h: The BPM: Detroit and Chicago club sounds, a cyborg on the cover
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.4 and ranked it No. 13 of 2025.
years.xp:
Stones Throw released it as her third album. Parks drew on her parents' Michigan and Illinois roots, with recording in both cities, and introduced an alter ego, Gadget Girl. Wikipedia lists Metacritic at 83; Album of the Year shows a 81 critic average.

NPR describes a grief-stricken woman meeting her digital avatar. Parks told NME the violin is very Black and that movement has become part of her self-care. One critic noted the concept pushes her violin to the back.

years.h: Tour with a violin guitar, dates into 2026
years.p: She built a custom "violin guitar" for the live show; North American dates run through January and February 2026.
years.xp: NME mentions the custom instrument and family collaboration with her twin sister and a cousin. Wikipedia lists the tour dates.
